depth_findings.text: execute_action (the existing write-path execute_provider_action client, around integration_tools.rs lines 369-451) still interpolates connection_id into the URL path without validation. Same retargeting risk as the reviewer's read finding. Not fixed here because it is outside the listed fixes; a follow-up for the lead to decide.
Egress hold cause is still RiskyEffectUnderAsk, not tainted_egress, until the WS13 vocabulary shared-edit lands. The approval a person sees names the wrong gate until then.
The screening taint is in memory only: a pause and resume segment starts a new loop without the flag.

The screening taint lives only in memory (ConnectorTaint in LoopContext, runtime_loop/mod.rs ~311). A pause and resume starts a new loop with a default taint, so after one person-approved egress call, later web_fetch or execute_provider_action calls in the resumed run are not held even though the flagged content is still in history. Needed before the flag is switched on.

execute_action (the write-path execute_provider_action client, integration_tools.rs ~369-451) still interpolates connection_id into the URL path with no is_connection_id check, the same retargeting risk the reviewer raised for reads.

In run_rounds, any read in a round holds egress calls in the same round (read_in_round), even when the read is clean. That is stricter than the DoD (after a read with screening taint or Flagged) and is not recorded as a deviation, while a clean read's egress in the next round is not held.

No test covers the held outcome end to end (an approval pause carrying the tainted_egress cause), and none covers a flagged read in round N holding web_fetch in round N+1. Only the pure function tainted_egress_held is unit-tested.
No permission-level test for read_provider_action: only a golden table row in permission/mod.rs:1252. The named permission test pattern and tests/autonomy_ladder_contract.rs are not extended.
read_action_json now validates connection_id (a behaviour change) but has no production callers in the tree, so its guard is covered only by tests; confirm it is intended or remove the dead function.
The tool is never offered in production: merged_tool_defs passes an empty connector_scope, which is correct until WS23-S4 lands, so the flag-on path is untested end to end until then.
